## Exact independent final assessment

Reviewed the complete integrated diff cf6ed229b8314727f47c6dbe387510b4f6f548ac..5e88a0397d0f1f5d57999ca338758a861c4ac9fa on release/v1, including version intent, Design/guidance, planning, implementation/tests and current assessment/evidence records. This assessor authored none of this initiative's Design, plan or code. Earlier work by this agent concerned a different initiative's independent Proposal assessments and did not author this contribution. This is a new final whole-change inspection after sole M1 closure, not substitution of its approved milestone review.

Current normative authority is Design Review r2's Release/guidance package, Delivery Review r5's exact current primary plan, and the adopted CLI/Workflow discovery/retirement contracts. Their normative member hashes match. Design r2's older plan identity is explicitly contextual allocation history; Delivery r5's three changed preimplementation test/selector subjects are supporting inspection, not normative implementation approvals. I assessed the actual changed implementations here; no old engineering judgment is retargeted. M1 implementation evidence's 28 engineering subjects match exactly, and the suffix after tested 09c1d089d02ae0ef53a03fe668c91d9c20563b8a contains only registry/evidence/M1 review recording. No contrary finding or blocker was found in current scope.

## Integrated behavior and no-finding rationale

Ordinary PR and main CI now share isolated pending-release preparation before returning to their existing selected/direct runners. Preparation validates the exact committed source, derives CI-only intent without pretending to observe public eligibility, uses the existing candidate builder and full verifier, restores the actual packed runtime/metadata and reports C and candidate identities. Effective original range resolves before entering C; checks use C as head while retaining the original base and source-change selection. Main retains all direct gates and execution order. The parent reruns ci_subject after checks, rejecting mutated source or packed/ignored runtime. Child exit 3 cannot be confused with the source-mode sentinel after a failed prepared run.

Candidate-only CI cannot authorize publication: approval validation explicitly rejects ci_only, while hosted preparation retains public-version/increment checks. The wrapper does not modify publication/provider behavior or grant credentials. Pending release validation is routed only for the verified workspace/current candidate tag; historical versions still use recorded-source validation. Lifecycle's pending-preflight exception checks the sealed subject and revision before relaxing only that current tag's pending requirement. Failed/unknown values, wrong roots/tags/revisions, missing/tampered proof and unrelated release records remain strict. This connects selected snapshot validation to actual prepared evidence without marking authored pending facts as successful publication.

Version 1.0.0 intent, package and lock agree. Breaking-record/command/skill changes explain the major decision; notes preserve explicit upgrade/adoption and publication limits. Current fixture expectations follow the tested package rather than a stale version, while incompatible and historical fixed cases remain fixed. The independently generated packed candidate, not invented source-tree metadata, supplies new-version archive/index identities to the package tests. Preparation-evidence.md retains its initial failed/blocked observations; these are historical preparation evidence and are not the current implementation pass or a claim of remote publication. Final Verify must explain the current outcome without rewriting those observations.

The small workflow-context change restores existing discovery classification before applying current-ID grammar. Safe directory inspection, archive/noncurrent exclusion without decoding, reserved/mixed malformed-current rejection, explicit invalid-ID rejection and limits remain intact. The retirement-ledger test projects only the already-disposed compact_contract.canonical inventory slot to current record_retirement.regression ownership, asserting old absence/new presence and retaining exact coverage, unique ownership and negative structural cases. Historical ledger bytes and runtime support remain unchanged. Changed ledger paths select actual current-retirement proof, whose repository-only Node test invokes the Python ledger suite and propagates failure. This is contract reconciliation exposed by real main CI, not equivalence of retired acceptance and current safe rejection or a blanket test waiver.

## First-pass checklist coverage

1. Spec alignment: pass. REL-SR-02/08/09/22–24 and plan M1 govern pending/prepared/historical selection and CI-only authority; CLI-SR-10/18/23 and WF-SR-10 govern the bounded existing-contract restorations.
2. Test coverage: pass. Exact-subject actual selected PR/direct main proof includes release/package/installed-target and governance consumers. Focused regressions protect unknown intent, CI-only approval, changed source/ignored runtime, arguments, child failure, private diagnostics, discovery and ledger distinctions. No selected test is removed.
3. Edge cases: pass. Tests and real composition distinguish pending/historical/current inputs; changed candidate and package overlays; main defaults/repeated range arguments; malformed proof and return-code sentinel; archive/noncurrent versus invalid current/residue stores. Public eligibility remains a separate hosted observation.
4. Error handling: pass. Preparation failure stops instead of falling back to a raw-source pass. Required runtime facts remain blocking; errors avoid private diagnostic paths. Missing/invalid prepared context is a bounded validation error. Existing public retry/recovery paths are not changed.
5. Architecture boundaries: pass. Reuses existing coordinator/candidate/full-verifier and CI runners. Source S, generated source C, build overlay and nonpublication identity remain explicit. Local record discovery does not infer approval or lifecycle meaning.
6. Compatibility: pass. Current-version fixtures change only version-dependent expectations; historical/incompatible cases, archived ledger and records retain their meaning. No new record format, runner or public release authorization is introduced. User-selected GitHub review-count policy remains distinct from repository independent review and release approval.
7. Security/privacy: pass. CI-only candidates fail publication approval, actual packed bytes and script/source identities are checked, no publication is run by CI preparation, and public dispatch redacts private path errors. Tests cover these changed boundaries; no new secret-bearing record/output was found.
8. Derived artifact currency: pass within the reviewed claim. Existing builder/full verifier generates actual archives, package metadata/index and tarball for tested C; checks consume those exact bytes. Authored source remains pending rather than presenting false generated identities. No public 1.0.0 publication/candidate reuse is claimed.
9. Unrelated changes: pass. Discovery/ledger fixes are explicitly allocated dependencies exposed by required main execution, with their existing owners and negative protection. Version intent is the authorized reproduced input. No speculative cleanup or historical rewrite was added.
10. Validation evidence: pass. Same final engineering source and base were used for actual PR and main commands; durable evidence records all failed/interrupted attempts separately. Logs and subjects corroborate the final passes; this review grants no hosted-CI or final Verify success.

## Actual checks and reliance

Independently executed during this final review:

- PYTHONPATH=scripts python -m unittest release_candidate_tests.ReleaseCandidateTests release_execution_tests.ReleaseApprovalTests release_coordination_tests.ReleaseCoordinationTests — 33 tests passed.
- node --test packages/rigorloop/test/workflow-context.test.js — 38 tests passed, zero failed/skipped.
- python scripts/test-retirement-ledger.py — 17 tests passed.
- git diff --check — passed.
- Exact current engineering/evidence and normative package identity comparison — matched; recording-only suffix inspected.

Inspected and relied on existing actual execution evidence rather than rerunning unaffected broad suites:

- bash scripts/ci.sh --mode pr --base cf6ed229b8314727f47c6dbe387510b4f6f548ac --head 09c1d089d02ae0ef53a03fe668c91d9c20563b8a — exit 0; selected checks include model, lifecycle, release, selector, broad-smoke and package/CLI proof.
- bash scripts/ci.sh --mode main --base cf6ed229b8314727f47c6dbe387510b4f6f548ac --head 09c1d089d02ae0ef53a03fe668c91d9c20563b8a — exit 0, all 28 direct checks passed.

Both logs identify prepared source 776e14d5b5930924d3e36bfc25be2c1036de2ee9. Their separately generated candidate IDs and actual receipts are recorded in m1-implementation. Each check run is assessed against its own exact sealed artifacts and receipts; no artifact identity is inferred from the shared C alone. Reuse is affirmative: all proved engineering surfaces are unchanged, tested commands ran against real prepared packages and no relevant failure contradicts the final result. Prior partial/failed attempts remain preserved rather than relabeled.

## Residual limits and handoff

This is not proof of npm OIDC authorization, remote deployment setup, public installation or publication success. Those require the real protected merged-source operation and its observed outcomes. Final Verify remains distinct and must assess current total readiness, evidence coherence and explanation. Return this recorded final judgment to the routing owner; no engineering, plan, work/activity, other findings or external state was changed by this review.
